name: Real Estate
description: Purchase, sale, development or financing of property to integrate illicit funds, taking advantage of high values, price opacity and the involvement of intermediaries. Techniques include buying with cash or via complex structures, rapid flipping, and mortgage fraud.

sources.text: FATF, Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing Through the Real Estate Sector (2007)
FATF and Egmont Group, Concealment of Beneficial Ownership (2018)
FATF, Guidance for a Risk-Based Approach: Real Estate Sector (2022)

indicators.name: Purchase price inconsistent with buyer's known means
indicators.canon: Wealth or spending inconsistent with known means
indicators.desc: Assets, lifestyle spending or purchases clearly exceed the customer's known legitimate income or declared wealth, with no verifiable source.
indicators.ctx: Property acquired is far beyond the buyer's declared income or wealth, with no verifiable source.
indicators.fp: Inheritance, business sale or gifts may explain.

indicators.name: Purchase through opaque company or trust
indicators.canon: High-value asset held through opaque vehicle
indicators.desc: Property, art, vessels or other valuables are acquired or held via a company, trust or storage arrangement with concealed beneficial owners.
indicators.ctx: Buyer is an offshore company, nominee or trust with hidden beneficial owners.
indicators.fp: Tax and estate planning vehicles are used.

indicators.name: Price materially above or below market
indicators.canon: Transaction price materially different from market value
indicators.desc: Price paid differs sharply from market value, comparable sales or estimates without commercial justification.
indicators.ctx: Declared price differs from valuation, followed by resale or loan at different value.

indicators.name: Rapid resale or flipping with no improvement
indicators.canon: Rapid resale or return of recently acquired asset
indicators.desc: An asset is bought and quickly resold or returned for a refund in a different payment form, with no apparent reason or improvement.
indicators.ctx: Property bought and sold in a short time at changing prices or with no apparent reason.

indicators.name: Large cash component or non-standard funding
indicators.canon: High-value purchases paid in cash, crypto or non-standard funds
indicators.desc: High-value assets are bought with cash, crypto, third-party or otherwise non-standard funding.
indicators.ctx: Part of purchase paid in cash, third-party transfers or unexplained funding routes.

indicators.name: Mortgage repaid early or from unusual sources
indicators.canon: Mortgage repaid early or from unusual sources
indicators.desc: Loan quickly settled in lump sum or by third parties.
indicators.ctx: Loan quickly settled in lump sum or by third parties.

indicators.name: Multiple properties bought by same person or nominees
indicators.canon: Multiple properties bought by same person or nominees
indicators.desc: Portfolio built through different names or relatives.
indicators.ctx: Portfolio built through different names or relatives.

indicators.name: Buyers or agents reluctant to provide information
indicators.canon: Buyers or agents reluctant to provide information
indicators.desc: Parties avoid face-to-face contact, deal via representatives or insist on speed.
indicators.ctx: Parties avoid face-to-face contact, deal via representatives or insist on speed.

indicators.name: High-risk jurisdiction funds or buyer connections
indicators.canon: Counterparty or flows in higher-risk jurisdictions with weak AML controls
indicators.desc: Funds, counterparties or institutions are located in jurisdictions with weak AML supervision, sanctions exposure or limited VASP regulation.
indicators.ctx: Funds or buyers come from jurisdictions with weak controls or sanctions exposure.
